context: 1. Confirm no session is mid-write: run sweep-stale, then re-read stats and check no foreign actor holds a live claim. 2. Take the rollback artifact: '_project/scripts/todo export --out DIR' writes items.jsonl + events.jsonl + index.md; keep it OUT of the repo. 3. Rehearse against a scratch local SQLite DB first: 'todo-db --db SCRATCH restore-legacy --project-id benchbox --input DIR --replace', then verify counts and 'audit verify' there. 4. Only once the rehearsal is clean, repeat against the hosted DSN. 5. Re-verify counts, claims and audit verify on the hosted DB. 6. Record the runbook, the credential change (TODO_DB_RO_AUTH_TOKEN) and the rollback procedure as an ADR under _project/decisions/.
description: The hosted tracker runs the embedded schema (meta.schema_version=3). todo-db >= 0.3 expects a schema_migrations table plus an event hash chain, so EVERY standalone command fails against it today: 'Hrana: SQLite error: no such table: schema_migrations'. It also wants hosted read credentials in TODO_DB_RO_AUTH_TOKEN alongside TODO_DB_AUTH_TOKEN. This blocks BOTH adoption paths - full CLI replacement and delegate-only routing of the standalone-only 'update' verb - so it must land before either. The DB is live and shared: at filing it holds 1627 items (42 active / 228 planning / 1333 done / 24 dropped) and 11 open claims across three actors (joe 8, codex 2, claude 1). Migration is destructive (restore-legacy --replace) and must not run while another session is mid-write. Supersedes the DB half of the dropped item adopt-todo-db-standalone-cli-for-amendable-items.

deferrals.reason: Found by rehearsing on a scratch SQLite DB, which is why the plan had a rehearsal step. The standalone's restore_legacy(snapshot: dict) at src/todo_db/database.py:463 requires a single JSON object containing 12 NORMALIZED tables: items, events, work_units, work_needs, item_deps, scope_rules, verifications, preserves, anti_patterns, prior_art, deferrals, meta. The legacy 'todo export' emits a DIRECTORY of items.jsonl + events.jsonl + index.md - 2 of the 12 - and items.jsonl is denormalized, carrying work, deps, scope, verifications, preserves, anti_patterns, prior_art and deferrals as nested collections. restore_legacy explicitly strips exactly those nested keys and expects them as separate tables, so the exporter's output is structurally invalid as importer input. The legacy CLI has no raw-table dump mode. Confirmed by running it: 'error: Extra data: line 2' when fed items.jsonl (it json.load's a single object), and 'Is a directory' when fed the export dir. The failure occurs at input parsing, before any write, so a live attempt would have failed safely - but it would have failed. Two further facts: the standalone now reports 'schema v4 ready', not the v3 this item assumed; and findings-schema-v4-lossless-legacy-fields is claimed and active in another session right now, so the destination schema is being changed concurrently.
deferrals.summary: No working export->restore-legacy path exists; the two formats do not line up
